players.product: memory test handlers & HBM cube probers

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook in the Q1 2026 IR book: the company attributes Q1 growth (preliminary revenue KRW 52,400M, operating profit KRW 9,702M) to a surge in DRAM/NAND demand lifting memory test-equipment sales plus higher COK and board parts sales, and expects DRAM/NAND demand to persist through Q2 and H2 so that revenue keeps growing after Q1; it expects continued Cube Prober orders from the customer it is already delivering to and additional orders from the customer that placed an initial order.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue KRW 52,400M; operating profit KRW 9,702M; revenue growth expected to continue in Q2 and H2

quarterly_data.signal: HBM Cube Prober status by customer: supplying mass-production units to Samsung Electronics with order volume rising; orders secured from SK Hynix with volume expected to rise; Micron is evaluating the equipment. Management's view: from HBM4E onward 100% inspection of individual dies becomes mandatory rather than a differentiator, and the Cube Prober is the most economical way to do it (fewer tools, lower power and maintenance cost). The deck also says Techwing expects to enter the co-packaged optics (CPO) inspection-equipment market (optical alignment, silicon photonics chip, mechanical/thermal and high-speed electrical tests), citing its ultra-precision control, sub-1nm vision and DLP handler technology.
quarterly_data.figure: Cube Prober: mass production at Samsung, orders secured at SK Hynix, evaluation at Micron
